question: Why did UK inflation spike in 2022?
summary: UK inflation rose in 2022: 5.4% (2021-12) -> 11.1% (2022-10 peak), +5.7 pts; 2020 average 0.8%. The evidence is consistent with these drivers: (1) household energy inflation (CPI housing, water & fuels) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak; (2) food inflation (CPI food & non-alcoholic drinks) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak; (3) the 12-month change in the pound's value against the dollar fell during the run-up to the 2022 peak.
supported: Household energy inflation (CPI housing, water & fuels) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
Food inflation (CPI food & non-alcoholic drinks) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
Transport inflation (CPI transport, incl. motor fuel) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
Services inflation (CPI services) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
The 12-month change in wholesale European gas prices rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
The 12-month change in the pound's value against the dollar fell during the run-up to the 2022 peak
UK short-term interest rates were low (average below 1%) in the 6-18 months before the 2022 peak
UK unemployment was at least 0.3 pts below its 2020 average in the 6-18 months before the 2022 peak

H1: Household energy inflation (CPI housing, water & fuels) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H2: Food inflation (CPI food & non-alcoholic drinks) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H3: Transport inflation (CPI transport, incl. motor fuel) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H4: Services inflation (CPI services) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H5: The 12-month change in wholesale European gas prices rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H6: The 12-month change in Brent crude oil prices rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H7: The 12-month change in global food commodity prices rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H8: The 12-month change in the pound's value against the dollar fell during the run-up to the 2022 peak
H9: UK short-term interest rates were low (average below 1%) in the 6-18 months before the 2022 peak
H10: UK unemployment was at least 0.3 pts below its 2020 average in the 6-18 months before the 2022 peak

reference: CPI rose to 11.1% in October 2022, the largest upward contributions from housing and household services (electricity and gas) and food (ONS, Consumer price inflation, October 2022).
